comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: Both versions preserve the self-curse involving the tongue and palate, the two negative conditions, remembrance of the feminine addressee Jerusalem, and Jerusalem's elevation above the speaker's joy. The lyric's 'stick' and 'roof of my mouth' retain the physical image in ordinary English.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: 'Highest joy' and 'greatest joy' interpret the Hebrew 'head of my joy' as supreme joy. The lyric's contractions and line breaks do not change the sense.

literal_backbone: May my tongue cling to my palate,
if I do not remember you,
if I do not raise Jerusalem above the head of my joy.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: above/upon; head, top, chief; my joy, gladness
word_notes.note: Both render the head/top metaphor as preeminence. 'Greatest' expresses rank rather than height, while 'lift ... above' retains the surrounding spatial imagery.
word_notes.rendered_as: Literal: 'above my highest joy'; lyric: 'above my greatest joy'

renderings.differentiator: Preserves both 'if I do not' clauses.
